why.1: Section 3.2 lists permissives P1-P9. Table 5.1 gives the start steps in order. Step 1 drives the slide valve to SP-12 (15%) before step 2 energizes the starter. The SP-22 (30 s) bypass of C1 and A-01 starts on SS-101 running feedback, which is stated explicitly and flagged in OI-11.
why.2: A start counter increments on step 2 entry over a rolling SP-36 (60 min) window with a limit of SP-35 (4). Permissive P3 blocks START. The HMI shows the failed permissive, the time until the next allowed start, and alarm A-15. FR-C101-025 tests this, and a minimum off time P4 is added.
why.3: T9 sends any state to ESD. Trip/ESD is priority-1 override, active in both AUTO and MANUAL. ESD stays active on HMI comms loss. C12 is 1oo2 with no delay. HS-130 is hardwired and works with the PLC in program mode or off (FR-C101-034). No bypass is defined, and reset needs a supervisor. Detector bad PV is defined in C14 and 8.1: EF-201 high speed, alarm A-22, and the healthy detector still trips. NE43 bad-signal limits are given.
why.4: Section 8.3: on power restore C-101 is in OFF with no automatic restart. Trip and ESD latches and the start count are retained, and A-25 is raised. FR-C101-001 and FR-C101-052 test this. Trips are latched and need an operator or supervisor RESET.
why.5: The 4.2 override table ranks the current overrides above AUTO/MANUAL demand. Load is blocked at 95% FLA (SP-27) and unload is forced at SP-29, each with release hysteresis. The overrides apply in both modes, and FR-C101-017 tests the priority, so suction control and current limit cannot fight.
why.6: Trips C1-C14 have cause, delay, effect, latch and reset. The alarm table does not give a reset or acknowledge method for any alarm. Several alarms have no delay (A-03 discharge temp high, A-20 at 25 ppm, A-05/A-07/A-08). The C1 reset description is muddled. So not every alarm and trip has tag, value, delay, action and reset in one-by-one checkable form.

why.1: The OUTPUT is only the tail of the document: setpoints SP-24 to SP-38, Appendix B and the pre-issue checks. It refers to Section 5 but contains no step-by-step start sequence. It does not show the slide valve being unloaded before start or the event that begins the 30 s low-oil bypass. OI-06 shows the bypass start point is still open.
why.2: SP-24 and SP-25 give 4 starts per rolling 60-minute window. There is no description of how the limit is enforced or what the operator sees when a start is blocked.
why.3: SP-31 to SP-33 define bad-signal limits and FR-C101-102 tests the HS-130 hardwired circuit with the PLC in PROGRAM mode. Neither states that the 150 ppm shutdown and the ESD cannot be overridden from the HMI. Detector fault behavior for AE-110A/B is not written out in the visible text.
why.4: The pre-issue check says power loss/restart is 'Met (Section 8)', but Section 8 is not in the OUTPUT. No no-auto-restart or latched-trip reset requirement is visible.
why.5: No description of how the current limit interacts with suction pressure control. Only OI-05 (FLA) is mentioned.
why.6: Only the ammonia setpoints are visible, with no delay, action or reset given for them. The oil, discharge temperature and suction trips are not listed with tag, value, delay, action and reset. Sections 6 and 7 are referenced but not included.

why.1: Section 5 lists 12 start permissives, including slide valve ≤15%. Section 6.1 gives a step table (S0–S4) with transitions and failure actions. S1 unloads the slide valve to ≤10% before S2 energizes RUN. Section 6.2 states the 30 s oil trip bypass is counted from the moment the RUN command is issued in S2.
why.2: Section 11 enforces 4 starts in a rolling 60-minute window by storing the last 4 start timestamps. Every RUN command counts, whether or not the start succeeds, and the history survives a power cycle. When a start is blocked the HMI shows 'Next start available in mm:ss', and 6.4 adds an 'Auto start blocked – starts/hr' message.
why.3: Section 3 says no HMI user at any level may bypass an ESD function in Section 10. Sections 10.1, 10.3 and 10.4 put the 150 ppm and break-glass shutdowns on hardwired paths independent of the PLC, and FAT tests 23 and 25 check this with the PLC in Program mode. Section 10.5 defines a detector fault (controller fault input, <3.5 mA or >21 mA) and its response: alarm, EF-201 high speed, starts blocked on a dual fault.
why.4: Section 12 covers power restoration: no automatic restart, all trips and the ESD state are retained, and the operator must reset and start manually. Auto-cycle resumes only after the 'Power restored' alarm is acknowledged. Output modules go to OFF on PLC fault. Section 3 defines trips as latched, requiring the condition to clear plus an operator reset.
why.5: Section 7.3 sets an override priority in which the current-limit forced unload and the load inhibit outrank normal AUTO or HAND control. Section 7.4 inhibits LOAD at ≥95% FLA in both modes, forces unload pulses at ≥98% FLA, and releases at <93% FLA with hysteresis, so the two controls do not fight.
why.6: Table 9.1 lists most C-101 alarms and trips with tag, setpoint, delay, action and reset, but it is not complete. The 25 ppm NH3 alarm is not in the table, and T-13 only says 'See 10.3'. 'EF-201 failed to start', 'Slide valve not responding' and the detector fault alarm appear only in prose, with no reset method and in some cases no delay.

why.1: Section 5 lists permissives P1–P13, including P9 (slide valve ≤5%). Section 6 gives a step-by-step sequence: unload to minimum first (6.1), then energize the run command, which starts the 30 s low-oil bypass timer at step 6.3 (C-101-RUN energized).
why.2: Section 9 defines a start counter with 4 timestamps in a rolling 60-min window, counted when RUN is energized (failed starts included). This feeds permissive P7. The HMI shows starts in the last 60 min and time until the next start, and the blocked permissive shows red. Power-cycle handling is also addressed.
why.3: ESD is hardwired and does not pass through PLC logic. The 150 ppm and ESD trips are active 'Always', all trips remain active in MANUAL, and trip setpoints are not HMI-adjustable. A hardwired 150 ppm relay is recommended. Section 10.4 defines responses for one or both detectors faulted, including out-of-range mA.
why.4: Section 13 says the compressor stays stopped after power restoration, with no automatic restart and a 'Restart Required' message; any auto restart is an OPEN item needing defined conditions. Section 10.1 latches trips and requires condition clear, operator Reset, then a new Start. F22 tests this.
why.5: The Section 7.2 priority table makes the current load inhibit at 95% FLA (release 92%) override normal suction control, with forced unload at 100% FLA as a backstop. Overrides apply in both modes and higher priority always wins, so the two loops do not fight. F12 and F13 test this.
why.6: Table 10.1 lists each alarm and trip with ID, tag, condition, setpoint, delay, active-when, action and reset. Table 10.2 does the same for gas levels (setpoint, delay, action, reset). FAT tests F6–F24 map to the individual items, so a tester can check them one by one.

why.1: FR-C101-004 lists every start permissive. Steps S1–S5 give a step-by-step start sequence with timeouts and failure responses. S2 unloads the slide valve to at or below SP-11 (15%) before S3 energizes the starter. The SP-17 30 s PDT-102 bypass is defined as starting from the run command, and S4/S5 then enable oil protection.
why.2: FR-C101-006 and FR-C101-007 define a rolling 60-min start counter. It counts at run-command-on, blocks the 5th start, and is retentive with a fail-safe on corruption. SP-30 adds a minimum stop-to-start time. When blocked, the operator sees ALM-C101-09, plus the start count, the time until the next start and the blocking permissive (section 9, FR-C101-037).
why.3: Detector fault and out-of-range behavior is defined (FR-C101-031, FR-C101-032, voting). Break-glass is hardwired and works with the PLC unpowered (FR-C101-002). However, nothing explicitly states that the 150 ppm ESD cannot be overridden or bypassed from the HMI or by any mode. FR-C101-001 only says trips do not depend on the HMI, and FR-C101-017 covers only the capacity Manual mode.
why.4: FR-C101-009 and FR-C101-034: after a power loss the PLC goes to ST0/ST5/ST6 with no automatic start and needs a new START. Latched trips and the first-out cause are kept in retentive memory and need RESET (FR-C101-008).
why.5: FR-C101-014 blocks load pulses at or above 95% FLA in both Auto and Manual, with hysteresis. FR-C101-015 forces unload in any mode at or above SP-22 until current is below 95%. This explicitly overrides suction-pressure load requests, so the two loops do not fight.
why.6: The trip table T1–T7 gives cause, delay (for some), effect and reset. The alarm table gives no delays and no per-alarm reset/acknowledge method; it relies on a generic FR-C101-030. ALM-C101-08 covers T1–T6 only and omits T7. Trip T3 and the E rows give no explicit delay. The list is therefore not fully checkable one by one with tag, value, delay, action and reset.

why.1: Section 3.2 lists ten start permissives, including ZT-105 at or below SP-10. In SQ-1, step 1 pulses ZY-105U to minimum before the motor starts, and failure returns to ST-1 with no motor start. In step 2 the run command and the 30 s bypass timer (SP-14) start together, and FR-C101-024 defines that the bypass timer begins when the run command energizes.
why.2: Enforced by a rolling-window start counter (SP-30 = 4 starts, SP-31 = 60 min), a minimum start-to-start interval (SP-32) and a retentive start history counted on the real-time clock. IL-07 blocks the start, and the HMI shows the time to next start plus alarm XA-101.
why.3: The SIS note says IL-04 and IL-05 open the motor run circuit and de-energize XV-120 through hardwired contacts that do not depend on the PLC. FR-C101-047 forbids reset from a remote or automatic source. Detector fault behavior is defined: one bad detector alarms and the other stays in service (FR-054); both bad applies IL-06 (FR-055); bad-PV limits are SP-37 and SP-38.
why.4: FR-C101-004 says the PLC enters ST-1, or ST-0 if a trip was latched, with no automatic start. FR-005 keeps trip latches in retentive memory. FR-061 keeps the gas shutdown latched. Trips need an operator reset once the cause is clear (T10).
why.5: Section 4.2 sets an override priority: forced unload, then load inhibit, then LC-101. Load is inhibited at 95% FLA (SP-22) with reset at 92%, and unload is forced at SP-24. Manual load commands are rejected during an override, so the two controls do not fight. Note that forced unload is set at 100% FLA, not at 95%.
why.6: The interlock table gives cause, delay, effect and reset for trips. The alarm table gives no delay and no reset method for any alarm, and the gas trip IL-04 has no delay. Values are references to SP numbers, so a tester must cross-check Appendix A. This is not a complete one-by-one checklist with tag, value, delay, action and reset for every item.

why.1: Section 5 lists the start permissives, including slide valve confirmed at minimum. Section 6 gives the start sequence step by step. Section 6.3 says the 30 s low-oil-trip bypass starts at the start command.
why.2: Section 6.4 defines a rolling 60-minute start record that blocks a fifth start. It counts failed attempts, survives a PLC power cycle, and restricts override to supervisor with logging. The HMI shows 'Start inhibited, starts/hour limit' and the time remaining.
why.3: Detector fault behavior is defined in 9.1 and the break-glass is hardwired and PLC-independent (9.4). However, the narrative never says the 150 ppm ESD cannot be overridden or bypassed from the HMI or in any mode. The HMI section also mentions logging of 'bypasses' without excluding the ESD from them.
why.4: Section 10.2 says there is no automatic restart after power is restored, and the unit restarts only on operator or AUTO demand within permissives. Section 10.3 retains trip states over a PLC power cycle. Section 8.1 says trips latch and need the cause cleared plus a manual HMI reset.
why.5: Section 7.5 inhibits load pulses at 95% FLA and forces unload above an adjustable higher threshold until current falls below 95%. It states the current limit takes precedence over suction demand to load, with an alarm on sustained high suction, so the two do not fight.
why.6: The summary table in Section 12 has no delay or reset-method columns. Delays appear only for some items in Section 8 (oil, suction, alarm defaults); TT-103 and the ammonia stages have no defined delays. Reset method is described separately and generically, so it is not checkable one by one per item.

why.1: Section 4 lists numbered start permissives, including the slide valve at or below 10% with a hold-and-unload if not. Section 5.1 gives a step-by-step start sequence. The 30 s low-oil bypass timer starts at a defined event: the moment the motor run command energizes.
why.2: Section 5.2 defines a rolling 60-minute start log that blocks a fifth start. The HMI shows 'Start Inhibited: Max starts/hour' and the time remaining. The limit applies in Hand and Auto, failed starts count, and resetting the count needs supervisor login. FAT test 20 covers it.
why.3: BG-1 is required to be hardwired and independent of the PLC. However, the 150 ppm ESD is never stated to act regardless of HMI mode or to be non-bypassable from the HMI; hardwiring it is only a 'design note' for the owner to decide. Detector fault behavior is also not defined: voting and whether a fault starts the 25 ppm action are left as [CONFIRM].
why.4: The narrative body has no power-loss or PLC-restart section. Only FAT test 30 says 'defined restart behavior; trips remain latched [CONFIRM]; no auto restart', without defining that behavior. It also does not address whether Auto mode can auto-start after power is restored.
why.5: Section 6.4 says load pulses are blocked at or above 95% FLA, overriding capacity-control load demand. The PLC pulses unload above a higher threshold (suggested 100%) until current is below 95%, and the inhibit clears at 93% for hysteresis. This applies in Auto and Hand, and the HMI shows a 'Load Limited' message, so the two functions do not fight.
why.6: The Section 10 summary table has tag, value, type, latched and action, but no delay or reset-method columns. Most delays are left as [CONFIRM] or 'a few seconds' rather than specified, so a FAT tester cannot check delay and reset for each item one by one.

why.1: The visible output is only the open-items table and status section. It claims every step has a timeout and failure response, but no startup steps, completion criteria or timeouts are shown (e.g., for failing to reach 500 rpm or an interrupted hold).
why.2: Nothing in the output says the 1600-1900 rpm band cannot be held, or what happens on an operator hold or a stall in the band. OI-05 only asks whether the vibration trip changes inside the band.
why.3: There is no coastdown description. OI-06 and OI-11 mention M-15 engagement and P-12 hardwired start logic only as open questions, and FR-ST1-305 suggests M-15 stops on low oil. Oil availability, DC backup during coastdown and turning-gear engagement at zero speed are not specified.
why.4: OI-04 defers the decision on which device executes each trip (Woodward or independent trip system). Overspeed protection is not explicitly allocated to the governor or hardwired protection anywhere in the visible text.
why.5: Trip reset requirements (latching, conditions to reset) are not shown, nor is the requirement that a restart after a trip goes back through the permissives. OI-10 only mentions sequence-of-events resolution for first-out.
why.6: The open-items table flags many items for confirmation rather than inventing values: cold-start criterion and warm/hot M-15 run time (OI-02), the hold-applicability assumption (OI-03), voting choices (OI-04), vibration measurement basis and behavior in the critical band (OI-05), M-15 engagement (OI-06), and SP-34 left TBD pending OEM data.

why.1: Startup steps FR-ST1-101 to 114 each give a transition condition, a timeout and a failure response. A 500 rpm ramp timeout goes to S7 with AL-ST1-011. A hold interrupted by an alarm goes to S4, and a hold timeout goes to S7.
why.2: FR-ST1-115/116/117 defer any hold requested inside 1600-1900 rpm until SP-CRIT-HI and reject in-band hold targets. Step 108 sets a minimum in-band ramp. FR-ST1-219 trips if the dwell exceeds SP-BAND-DWELL, which covers a stall. FR-ST1-301 continues to SP-CRIT-HI on comms loss.
why.3: P-11 is in standby and auto-starts on low PT-210, independent of sequence state (FR-ST1-201/203). P-12 backs up at 0.7 barg and runs through rundown (FR-ST1-202, FR-ST1-303). M-15 auto-starts in S0/S7 once speed is below zero and lube pressure is established (FR-ST1-011).
why.4: FR-ST1-221 puts trip logic in the Woodward or a dedicated hardwired trip system, outside the DCS. The mechanical bolt is independent and a hardwired watchdog is specified. OI-05 confirms overspeed is independent of the governor control path. Overspeed is not in the DCS sequence.
why.5: All trips are latched. FR-ST1-222 holds first-out cause and time until reset. Each trip row gives its reset conditions, with engineer login where required. S0 returns to S1 only after reset, and a new START repeats the permissive steps 101-105.
why.6: Proposed values are marked 'confirm' against the vendor manual. OI-02 covers warm/hot start holds and ramps. FR-ST1-233 defines 2oo2 behavior with one failed probe, and OI-06 asks to confirm the 2oo2 intent and the pk-pk basis. Other open items cover missing tags, voting and bearing temperature, and the added trips are disclosed.

why.1: Only Step 1 has a timeout and failure action (pressure not reached in a set time leads to a hold and an alarm), and Step 2 says the timer resets if M-15 or oil pressure is lost. Step 3 (vacuum, drains, gland steam) and Step 5 (synchronization) give no timeout or failure action. Step 4 does not say what happens if 500 rpm or 2000 rpm is not reached within a time. Hold interruption is only partly covered: timers run only while speed is within tolerance.
why.2: Section 1.7 inhibits any setpoint hold in 1600-1900 rpm and fixes a minimum ramp rate. An operator hold request inside the band continues through to 2000 rpm. A 'no-hold violation' alarm is raised if speed stays in the band longer than the expected transit time, which covers a stall.
why.3: Sections 2.1 and 2.8 say the turbine coasts down with P-11 and P-12 remaining available. Section 2.3 has P-12 (DC) auto-start below 0.7 barg as backup to P-11 (AC). M-15 is re-engaged only at zero speed, as a permissive.
why.4: Section 2.1 states trips act through the governor/trip system, are hardwired to close the ESV and control valves, and do not depend on DCS communication. Electronic overspeed is in the Woodward governor with independent probes, plus the mechanical bolt; none of it sits in the DCS.
why.5: Trips are latching with the first-out cause recorded. Reset requires the cause to clear plus an operator reset, and reset is blocked while a trip condition is active. Any trip returns the sequence to Step 0, so restart goes back through the pre-start permissives.
why.6: Missing data is marked [TBC] throughout and collected in section 5: warm/hot start criteria, alarm setpoints (example values are labelled TBC), and timer pause rules. Section 2.5 explicitly notes that with one faulted probe 2oo2 cannot trip, so the bearing is unprotected. It also flags the tight 110%/111% overspeed margin.

why.1: The step table gives an exit condition for every step, but no step has a timeout or failure action. Nothing covers 500 rpm not being reached, 2000 rpm not being reached, PT-210 not reaching normal, or sync failure. The only timeout is the critical-band stall alarm. Hold interruption is covered only generically: alarms pause the sequence and freeze the timer.
why.2: Section 1.4 says hold or setpoint requests inside 1600-1900 rpm are rejected and the ramp continues. A stall in the band raises a DCS alarm after a timeout, and the operator must continue or shut down. Section 1.5 adds that a pause does not hold in the band.
why.3: Section 2.6 keeps P-11/P-12 running for coast-down. Section 2.1 says pumps must not stop on trip and that P-12 auto-starts on DC below 0.7 barg as backup to P-11. Section 2.6 also has the turning gear engage automatically, only at zero speed.
why.4: Section 1.1 states trip functions are hardwired or in the Woodward/trip system and must not depend on the DCS. Section 2.2 places electronic overspeed in the Woodward acting directly on the trip solenoids, with the mechanical bolt as backup. P-12 start is hardwired on DC.
why.5: Permissive 1 requires no active trip and a reset trip latch, so a latched trip is reset through the permissives before restart. Section 2.6 specifies first-out annunciation and reset only after the condition clears and the turbine is in a safe state. Section 1.5 sends a trip to the tripped state, with restart based on thermal state.
why.6: Missing data is marked [TBC] throughout: warm/hot start rules, rates, transmitter counts, PT-220 alarm, and M-15 disengage method. It flags the 2oo2 vibration weakness (a single probe with a real fault cannot trip; a faulted probe is hidden), the narrow 0.1 barg and 36 rpm margins, and collects open items in section 3.

why.1: Section 4.4.4 defines a three-stage split-range on AIC-502 with split points SPL-532/533. A stage table gives each element's value in every output band: agitator 80-140 rpm first, then air 0-10 slpm with the agitator held at max, then O2 0-5 slpm with air at max. FR-BR500-042 requires the reverse order on DO rise, and FR-BR500-044 covers a stage that does not follow its setpoint.
why.2: The A/B deviation limits and delays are defined (SPL-507/508 for pH, SPL-524/525 for DO). One unhealthy probe triggers a bumpless switch to the healthy probe (FR-BR500-011). On disagreement, control continues on the selected PV and the operator picks the probe that agrees (FR-BR500-014). Alarms ALM-503/513 cover deviation and ALM-504/514 cover probe failure.
why.3: ALM-506 warns at the 36 L pre-limit (SPL-515). I-501 stops P-520 and latches the base-side lockout at 40 L with no bypass. FR-BR500-034 and SEQ-501 state that only SEQ-501 at the start of Media Fill resets FQI-521.
why.4: On Hold, the loops continue (FR-BR500-003). On STOP/ABORT, the loops keep their state and the system prompts for SEQ-503 (FR-BR500-004). On transition to Harvest, SEQ-503 runs automatically: P-520 stops, FCV-510/511/512 go to zero flow, SIC-530 is released holding its last speed, and the loops go INACTIVE.
why.5: The output never addresses that CO2 sparge affects dissolved gas or DO, and states no interaction or limit between the pH and DO loops. The only shared-gas logic is the I-506 overpressure override, which is not a pH/DO interaction.
why.6: FR-BR500-090 has the system refuse a Production setpoint change until a reason is entered. FR-BR500-091 requires the audit trail to record user ID, date, time, tag, old value, new value and reason, with OQ tests for both.

why.1: Section 4.3 sets three OP regions with breakpoints DO-12 and DO-13. SIC-530 ramps from AG-01 to AG-02 first. Air starts only when agitation is at maximum, and O2 starts only when air is at maximum. FR-DO-012 reverses the order on decreasing OP. Limits are given (AG-01/02, FL-01/02, FR-DO-013).
why.2: Section 4.1 defines the probe validity criteria. PH-07/DO-06 set the deviation alarm threshold and PH-08/DO-07 set the shed-to-FAULT threshold, each with a delay. When one probe is invalid, control uses the valid probe. On disagreement the current source is kept and an offline sample prompt is raised. Alarms A-PH-04/A-DO-04 and A-PH-03/A-DO-03 are defined.
why.3: A-BA-01 alarms at the BA-02 pre-limit (36 L). Interlock I-01 stops P-520 at BA-01 (40 L) and latches for the rest of the batch. FR-BA-001 resets WQI-521 once per batch, in SEQ-01 step 2 of the first Equilibrate, with no second reset on restart. The total persists across controller restart.
why.4: Section 3.3 and FR-BR-004 state that a HOLD does not change module state or outputs. STOP/ABORT drives both modules to INACTIVE (T-06, FR-BR-005). SEQ-02 handles the move to Harvest. Section 3.4 gives the final positions: P-520 stopped, FCV-510/511/512 at zero flow, and SIC-530 released to the Harvest phase at current speed.
why.5: The output does not address CO2 sparge as a shared influence on pH and dissolved gas, and it does not state any pH/DO loop interaction or limit (for example, air sparge stripping CO2 and raising pH). The only CO2 remark is the fault-position rationale for pH. The total gas flow limit is deferred to OI-05.
why.6: FR-GMP-001 to 005 make the system enforce the reason prompt before the change applies. Cancelling leaves the value unchanged. User authentication is required. The record holds user ID, time, tag, old and new value, and reason, and goes to the audit trail and batch record. Records cannot be edited.

why.1: Section 7.1 splits the AIC-502 output into three ranges with breakpoints at 33.3% and 66.7% and gives each actuator's range. DO-012 and DO-013 say a stage moves only when the previous one is at maximum. DO-014 sets the reverse unwind order, and DO-011, DO-016 and DO-017 cover limits and anti-windup.
why.2: PH-001 to PH-007 define probe health and a 0.10 pH deviation threshold for 60 s. They specify the PV used in each case: average, single healthy probe, or operator selection on disagreement. They also define the alarms (MEDIUM for single probe, HIGH for deviation, HIGH for total loss). DO-001 applies the same logic with a 10% threshold.
why.3: PH-022 raises an alarm at 36 L. PH-023 and PH-024 stop and interlock P-520 at 39.5 L in all modes. PH-020 and PH-026 reset the totalizer only at the start of Equilibrate of a new batch, with no operator reset mid-batch. PH-028 keeps the totalizer monotonic.
why.4: GEN-005 says control continues on HOLD. GEN-006 gives a concrete proposed Abort behaviour: continue control and raise a HIGH alarm, marked TBC. GEN-004 and Table 3-1 define the Harvest transition: controllers to MAN, CO2/O2/air at 0 slpm, base pump stopped, agitator released to phase control.
why.5: Section 8 states that air/O2 sparge strips CO2 and raises pH, and that CO2 sparge adds gas volume and lowers DO partial pressure. It also flags a total sparge flow limit of 17 slpm against the bag rating.
why.6: GEN-011 to GEN-013 require the system to demand a reason before accepting a Production setpoint change. A blank reason is rejected and a cancelled dialog keeps the old value. Each change is recorded in the Event Chronicle and batch record with user ID, time, old/new value, reason and batch ID.

why.1: Section 5.6.1 maps DOIC-502 output to each element with breakpoints at 0, 33.3, 66.7 and 100%. DO-12 and DO-13 state when the next stage may start (agitator at 140 rpm, air at 10 slpm). DO-14 defines reverse-order release, and DO-15 clamps each element to its range.
why.2: PM-15 sets a disagreement threshold (0.10 pH or 10% air saturation for 60 s) and raises a 'probe deviation' alarm. PM-13 uses the single healthy probe and raises a 'single probe control' alarm. PM-16 keeps control on the average while the probes disagree. PM-14 covers the case where both probes fail.
why.3: PH-23 raises a warning at 36 L. PH-24 stops P-520 at 40 L, interlocks it off for the rest of the batch and raises an alarm. The totaliser is reset at the start of Equilibrate (§5.3 table, PH-20 W_ref). PH-25 allows the interlock to be reset only by starting a new batch, with no override.
why.4: Hold (continue in Auto) and Harvest (gas valves at 0, P-520 stopped, controllers to Manual) are defined. Stop/Abort behaviour is left as an unresolved [TBC] choice between options. The agitator's final state in Harvest is deferred to an unspecified section (§[x]). The required final states are therefore not fully stated.
why.5: The output never addresses that CO2 sparge also affects dissolved gas or DO, nor any interaction or limit between the pH and DO loops. The only related point is open item 12 on a combined sparge limit, which is about foaming and filter capacity, not loop interaction.
why.6: SP-01 makes a reason mandatory before a Production setpoint change is accepted, via DeltaV e-signature/confirm. SP-02 leaves the setpoint unchanged if the reason is cancelled or blank. SP-03 requires the audit trail to record user ID, date/time, tag, old/new value, reason, batch and phase.

why.1: The visible output lists only cascade parameters (DO_OUT_A1 30%, DO_OUT_A2 70%, DO_SAT_TIME, SIC530 80–140 rpm). It never states when agitation hands over to air or air to O2, or how stages hand back.
why.2: Thresholds (PH_PROBE_DEV, DO_PROBE_DEV with delays) and alarms (AL-11, AL-12) are given. What the controller uses when one probe is bad or the probes disagree is only referenced (FR-BR500-102 to 104, IL-05/06, DO HOLD) and never actually defined in the visible text.
why.3: BASE_WARN is 32 L, before the limit. P-520 stops at BASE_LIMIT minus BASE_STOP_MARGIN, and the stop latches until the next batch with no operator reset. The base total survives restart. This is close to the expectation, though reset at batch start is only implied by 'until the next batch'.
why.4: It says only that Hold, Stop and Abort do not disable control, and leaves that as an open item. It gives no behaviour on transition into Harvest and no final state of the valves, pump and agitator at end of control.
why.5: No visible statement addresses CO2 sparge affecting dissolved gas or any interaction or limit between the pH and DO loops.
why.6: A system prompt for reason entry (SEQ-2), a reason list, a record-write-failure alarm and batch-record persistence are present. The required record fields (user, time, old and new value) are not specified in the visible text.

why.1: Section 4 splits DO demand into three stages with defined breakpoints: DO_S1_END=40% and DO_S2_END=70%, each with its actuator range. FR-BR500-017 requires SIC-530 to reach AGIT_MAX before FCV-511 opens, and FCV-511 to reach AIR_MAX before FCV-512 opens. FR-BR500-018 reverses that order on falling demand with an AGIT_MIN floor. FR-BR500-019 adds a rate limit.
why.2: Disagreement thresholds are defined: PH_PRB_DEV 0.10 pH and DO_PRB_DEV 10%, each with a delay. Alarms AL-04/AL-15 cover disagreement. FR-BR500-044 says control continues on the average and prompts PR-02 for probe selection. FR-BR500-039/041 use the healthy probe when one is bad, with AL-05/AL-16. IL-04/IL-05 handle both bad.
why.3: AL-08 warns at BASE_WARN (32 L). IL-01 trips at BASE_LIM minus BASE_MARGIN, stops P-520, blocks Manual start, latches through power loss and raises AL-09. The base total resets only on a new batch ID (FR-BR500-007, IL-01 reset), and SEQ-1 initializes it at start.
why.4: Hold: loops and outputs continue unchanged. Abort: immediate safe state with FCV-510 and FCV-512 closed, P-520 off, and FCV-511 and SIC-530 released at their last value. Harvest: loops go Out of service via Complete and SEQ-2, which defines the final valve, pump and agitator states.
why.5: No requirement states the effect of CO2 sparge on dissolved gas or DO, or any limit between the pH and DO loops. Only open item OI-10 mentions assessing CO2 stripping by air sparge and total gas flow, which defers the issue rather than specifying it. IL-07 covers acid/base interaction only.
why.6: FR-BR500-022 and SEQ-4 enforce a system prompt (PR-04) with a mandatory reason. Without a reason the change is cancelled. The system writes a record with batch ID, phase, parameter, old value, new value, time, user and reason before applying the change, and keeps the old value if the write fails.

why.1: DO-11 to DO-17 define when each stage engages: air only once SIC-530 is at 140 rpm, O2 only once air is at 10 slpm. They define reverse-order unwinding (O2 to 0, then air to 0, then agitator back toward 80 rpm) and clamp limits (80–140 rpm, 10 slpm, 5 slpm). Hysteresis is TBD, but the takeover and handback logic is defined.
why.2: PH-12/PH-14 and DO-02/DO-03 cover single-probe failure (use the healthy probe, raise an alarm) and a deviation alarm, with control continuing on the average. However, the A/B disagreement threshold and time delay are left as [TBD] for both pH and DO, so no defined threshold is given.
why.3: PH-32 sets a warning alarm before the limit (threshold TBD, 80% = 32 L suggested). PH-33 stops and locks out P-520 at 40 L with a high-priority alarm. PH-31 initializes the totalizer at batch start, persists it through Hold/Restart and bars operator reset during the batch.
why.4: Hold, Abort and Stop behavior (PH-05) is entirely [TBD], including agitation and gas flows. Harvest (PH-02) closes the valves and stops P-520, but only says SIC-530 is 'not driven by the DO cascade', so the agitator's final state is undefined.
why.5: IX-01 only says each loop is independent with no cross-compensation, and IX-02 leaves total sparge limits [TBD]. It does not recognize that CO2 sparge affects dissolved gas or DO, and it defines no actual interaction limit.
why.6: SP-01 to SP-04 require the system to demand a reason before a Production setpoint change takes effect and to reject the change if no reason is entered. The system records tag, old and new value, time, user ID and reason in a non-editable electronic batch record.

why.1: Section 6.2 and REQ-6.2.1 to 6.2.6 define the handoffs. Air sparge starts only when the agitator is at 140 rpm. O2 sparge starts only when air is at 10 slpm. On the way down, stages hand back in reverse order (O2, then air, then agitator). Ranges are clamped and transitions are bumpless. Hysteresis is left TBD.
why.2: Single-probe failure uses the healthy probe and raises an alarm. However, the A/B disagreement threshold and time delay are TBD (REQ-5.1.4, 6.1.4). What the controller uses when the probes disagree is also TBD, so deviation handling is not defined.
why.3: REQ-5.3.4 requires a pre-limit warning alarm (value TBD). REQ-5.3.2 and 5.3.3 stop and inhibit P-520 at 40 L with an alarm, and the operator cannot reset this during the batch. REQ-5.3.6 resets the totalizer only at the start of a new batch.
why.4: REQ-4.3 sends outputs to the inactive state (valves closed, pump stopped) on transition to Harvest. Hold, Abort and Stop are lumped together and marked TBD to confirm, with no distinct Hold behavior. The agitator's final state is explicitly deferred as TBD.
why.5: REQ-6.2.8 says the CO2 and DO sparges act independently with no override. It does not recognize that CO2 sparge affects dissolved gas or DO. The total gas flow limit is left TBD.
why.6: REQ-7.2 and 7.3 require a system-enforced mandatory reason field during Production. Changes without a reason are rejected. The record includes parameter, old and new value, time, user ID and reason. REQ-7.4 requires a non-editable audit trail.

why.1: SEQ-2 and SEQ-3 stage on measurable criteria. Stage-up is at SP-12 (90% load) for SP-13 (15 min), CHWST deviation SP-16/SP-17, or DP deviation with pumps at maximum. Stage-down is at SP-14 (80% of remaining capacity) for SP-15 (20 min). SP-20/SP-21 set chiller minimum run and off times, enforced by FR-CHW-032 and FR-CHW-059.
why.2: The minimum flow loop modulates FCV-701 from FIT-702 with setpoint = running chillers × 960 gpm × (1 + SP-07). It holds position while STARTING. SEQ-2 step 4 raises the setpoint and proves flow before the new chiller starts, and SEQ-3 step 5 lowers it after a stop. FR-CHW-055 and SEQ-2 step 4 open FCV-701 fully and alarm on low flow.
why.3: SEQ-4 detects the trip, latches the chiller UNAVAILABLE, and resets CHWST. It then starts the standby chiller from SEQ-2 step 2, which opens valves, starts the CHWP and CWP, raises minimum flow and adds a tower cell. Delays are skipped, and pumps stay under DP and minimum flow control. FR-CHW-087 alarms the trip, and FR-CHW-098 alarms if recovery is not met.
why.4: Reset is trim-and-respond, not linear. CHWST rises only if the highest valid coil valve position, including all surgery AHU valves, is below 85%, and it is lowered when any valve is above 95%. CHWST is forced to 42 F if any surgery valve signal is bad or in reduced capacity. A humidity ceiling is assigned to OI-05.
why.5: FR-CHW-065 says that on plant controller failure, equipment holds last state, VFDs go to fallback speeds SP-10/SP-30, FCV-701 fails open and isolation valves hold position. FR-CHW-067 has the plant controller run alone if the supervisory network is lost. FR-CHW-063 uses hardwired status on chiller comms loss.
why.6: FR-CHW-004 defines rotation criteria: lowest runtime on start, highest on stop, and an operator can fix the lead. However, the output never states that rotation must not reduce running capacity, for example make-before-break when swapping lead. That protection is only implicit because rotation happens at staging events.

why.1: The output is a truncated tail (sections 10-12) and contains no staging criteria, thresholds, delays, or minimum on/off times; staging is only referenced indirectly (SP IDs, OI-02/OI-09 'staging logic' still to settle).
why.2: No minimum flow control logic using FCV-701 and FIT-702 is shown; FIT-702 appears only in an open item about piping location, and staging-transition flow behavior is not defined.
why.3: Prompt P-01 states 'CH-n tripped. The standby chiller started' and references SEQ-D, implying auto-start with alarm, but the actual sequence including pump and tower sequencing is not present in the output.
why.4: Only OI-05 mentions confirming humidity limits for the 'CHWST reset hold (FR-CHW-024)'; the reset hold/limit logic based on critical valve position is not defined in the output.
why.5: No BAS controller or network failure behavior is described; P-05 covers power-loss restart only, and OI-04 defers restart behavior to the vendor.
why.6: Only 'chiller start order and maintenance flag' as operator-changeable items; no rotation criteria (runtime, schedule) or requirement that rotation not drop running capacity.

why.1: Section 5 sets stage-up at load >90% of enabled capacity, CHWST >1.5°F above setpoint with chillers at ≥95% FLA, or DP unmet at 95% pump speed, each for 10 min. Stage-down is at load <75% of remaining capacity for 15 min. Minimum run is 20 min, minimum off is 15 min, and max starts per hour follow the manufacturer.
why.2: Section 7.2 has FCV-701 modulated by PID on FIT-702 to hold a minimum flow setpoint of 960 gpm × operating chillers × 1.1. During start/stop transitions the valve goes to a preset open position. On FIT-702 loss it goes to a fixed open position. Section 7.3 adds low-flow protection below 960 gpm per chiller.
why.3: An operating chiller trip triggers immediate stage-up with no delay (5.2). The failure table isolates the tripped chiller, starts the standby chiller and pump, and raises a critical alarm. The start sequence (5.5) includes condenser pump start, flow proof, and tower enable.
why.4: The trim-and-respond reset weights requests from critical (surgery) air handlers more heavily. It locks reset to 42°F on high humidity or dewpoint in a critical zone, on failure of a critical AHU sensor, or when the plant is at N capacity. It is also disabled after staging. The output explicitly notes the dehumidification risk for surgical suites.
why.5: Section 9 says that if the BAS controller fails, chillers and pumps keep running locally at their last commanded state and standalone controllers hold the last good setpoint. Section 2 requires all sequences to run in the local controllers if communication with the workstation is lost.
why.6: Rotation criteria are defined: equal runtime, weekly changeover, unavailable units skipped, and no rotation during alarms or staging. However, the output never states that rotation brings the new lead online before stopping the old one or otherwise keeps running capacity intact. The no-capacity-drop requirement is not explicitly addressed.

why.1: Section 5 gives measurable stage-up criteria: load above 90% for 10 min, CHWST more than 1.5 °F over setpoint with chillers at or above 95% FLA, and pumps at 100% with DP low. Stage-down requires load below 75% of the remaining chillers' capacity for 15 min. Section 5.4 sets a 20 min minimum between stage changes, which guards against short cycling, and the manufacturer restart timers are respected.
why.2: Section 7 sets the minimum flow setpoint at 960 gpm times the number of operating chillers. FCV-701 is modulated by PID on FIT-702. Section 7.4 and step 6 of Section 4 define the transitions: the setpoint rises at the start command and falls only after the stopping chiller is isolated. FIT-702 failure handling and a per-chiller low-flow safety are also covered.
why.3: Sections 5.2 and 10.1 start the standby chiller immediately on a trip, with no delay. The start follows the Section 4 sequence, which covers CWP, tower enable and CHWP proving, and raises a high-priority alarm. Pre-opened standby paths are also specified.
why.4: Section 8.3 stops reset from rising and drives the setpoint back toward 42 °F when any surgery or critical AHU valve is above 90% open, has a space humidity high alarm, or has a discharge air temperature alarm. Reset is also disabled when outdoor dewpoint is above 60 °F, when N+1 is lost, and in failure modes.
why.5: Section 10.4 says chillers keep running independently on internal controls on BAS communication failure. VFDs and valves hold their last state or a safe default, FCV-701 fails to preserve minimum flow, and isolation valves fail as-is.
why.6: Section 3.2 rotates the lead by accumulated runtime every 7 days or on operator command. Rotation is make-before-break: the new chiller is started and proven loaded before the old one stops, so running capacity is not dropped.

why.1: R-02 flags that 'fixed setpoint' contradicts the MOV reset and that the contractor cannot implement both. It states one strategy: MOV resets the PIC-920 setpoint between SP-HDR-MIN and SP-HDR-MAX, with SP-HDR-INIT used at start and when MOV is disabled.
why.2: R-03 says closing the valve stops aeration and mixing, risking septic conditions and a permit excursion. It proposes holding the last good output for DO-BADPV-HOLD, then driving to POS-FALLBACK (last good output or 50%), and raising an alarm.
why.3: R-01 converts 7.5 psig to about 207.6 inH2O and 160/165 inH2O to about 5.78/5.96 psig. It explains that header pressure at setpoint always exceeds the stage-off value, so staging thresholds and setpoint conflict.
why.4: R-06 flags the missing surge protection and calls for a blow-off valve or minimum IGV position with a surge line. It also covers all FCVs closing and proposes a minimum header flow or blocking FCV closure below POS-MIN. R-03 notes that closing all valves deadheads the blowers into surge.
why.5: R-04 flags simultaneous restart causing combined inrush, restart of a coasting rotor, surge, and unexpected starts with personnel present. It proposes per-blower selectable auto-restart, one-at-a-time starts at RESTART-STAGGER intervals, and owner confirmation.
why.6: R-07 says the vibration trip has no tag, value, delay, latch or reset. R-08 questions the discharge-valve-open permissive, noting that starting into a live header needs a check valve and an open blow-off to avoid surge, and adds a blow-off-open permissive.

why.1: R-01 calls item 2 a contradiction: the setpoint cannot be both 'fixed at 7.5 psig' and reset by MOV logic. It gives one strategy: the PIC-920 setpoint is remote-set by MOV logic, clamped between min and max (SP-04/05), with 7.5 psig as the initial/fallback value only (SP-03).
why.2: R-05 states that closing the valve starves the basin, causing anoxic/septic conditions and permit risk. It proposes setting AIC-90x to manual, holding the last good output or going to the SP-07 fallback, and alarming. FR-AER-020 repeats this.
why.3: R-02 flags psig vs inH2O and says 160/165 inH2O is about 5.8/6.0 psig, well below the 7.5 psig setpoint. It notes the stage-on condition can never occur at the stated setpoint.
why.4: R-11 flags that no surge protection or minimum flow is defined. It ties the risk to MOV logic lowering pressure with valves at minimum, and calls for blow-off control or a vendor surge controller. R-05 also notes blowers can deadhead and surge if several valves close.
why.5: R-06 flags inrush (critical on a standby generator), restart before coast-down, surge risk and no warning to personnel. It proposes a restart-pending state with staggered one-at-a-time restarts through the normal sequence, made operator-selectable.
why.6: R-07 says item 7 has no tag, value, delay, latch/reset or trip action. R-09 says the discharge valve is untagged and ambiguous, notes many multistage centrifugal vendors need blow-off open at start, and calls for confirming the start line-up with the blower vendor.

why.1: Critical item 1 notes the header setpoint is called both 'fixed at 7.5 psig' and reset by MOV logic, calling these two different strategies. It states one clear choice, 'almost certainly MOV reset', and lists what that option needs.
why.2: Item 4 says closing the valve 'starves the basin', causing loss of nitrification, a possible permit excursion and solids settling. That is oxygen deprivation, though the words anoxic or septic are not used. It proposes holding the last good position or an operator-set fallback flow, alarming the failure, and enforcing a minimum airflow.
why.3: Item 2 converts 7.5 psig to about 208 inH2O and 160/165 inH2O to about 5.8/6.0 psig. It explains that header pressure would always sit above 165 inH2O, so blowers would keep staging off, meaning the thresholds and setpoint disagree.
why.4: Surge detection and protection is listed as missing and called essential for multistage centrifugal blowers. A blow-off/bypass valve is mentioned. Item 4 ties valve closure to the risk of deadheading the blowers and causing surge. The link to MOV logic lowering flow is not stated explicitly, but the valve-closure flow-drop risk is covered.
why.5: Item 5 flags unannounced restarts as dangerous to staff, simultaneous restart as able to overload a generator or exceed inrush limits, and restarting a spinning machine as a hazard. It proposes operator-selectable auto-restart, one-at-a-time staggered starts, and permissive re-checks.
why.6: Item 6 says the vibration trip needs a tag, alarm and trip setpoints, a time delay and a manual reset method. Item 7 says starting with the discharge valve open may cause surge, notes many vendors require a blow-off/bypass open at start, and asks for confirmation with the manufacturer.
